chapter_title: Open File Formats and Version Control
learning_objective: The learner will identify the HTML tag behind each of eight parts of a web page from a description of how the part looks, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** html-page-anatomy
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify the HTML tag behind each of eight parts of a web page from a description of how the part looks, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** HTML, Markdown, Source Format (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the marker that matches a visual hint. A click is correct when it matches the marker named in the Hint column of Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Hovering in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The picture's alt text is shown on the page. (2) Any large text is a heading tag. (3) A link needs no address. **Instructional Rationale:** Identifying the parts of a page is a Remember-level task, and an illustration links each visible part to the tag that creates it. The quiz asks the learner to go from the look to the tag, which is the direction a reviewer works when inspecting a source. **Content:** The illustration is a text-free flat drawing of a simple lesson web page inside a browser frame. A small tab sits at the upper left of the frame. On the page, from top to bottom, are a large bar of heading text, a block of several thin text lines, a landscape picture box with a thin strip beneath it, a short list of three lines each with a dot at its left, an underlined bar of link text, and a small grid of two columns and three rows. The eight markers: | # | Label | Hint (describes the look, not the name) | Description | Tip | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Page title (title tag) | A small tab at the upper left of the browser frame. | The title tag holds the text that appears in the browser tab and in search results. | Give each page its own title. | | 2 | Main heading (h1 tag) | The largest bar of text at the top of the page. | The h1 tag marks the page's main heading. A page usually has one. | Use heading tags in order, with no skipped levels. | | 3 | Paragraph (p tag) | A block of several thin lines under the heading. | The p tag marks a paragraph of text. | Keep one idea in each paragraph. | | 4 | Image (img tag) | The landscape picture box in the middle of the page. | The img tag shows a picture. Its alt attribute holds the text description for people who cannot see it. | Write alt text for every image that carries meaning. | | 5 | Caption (figcaption tag) | The thin strip directly beneath the picture. | The figcaption tag holds the caption for a figure, which is a good place to credit the image. | Put the image credit in the caption. | | 6 | Bulleted list (ul and li tags) | Three short lines, each with a dot at its left. | The ul tag marks a bulleted list, and each li tag is one item. | Use a real list tag, not dots typed by hand. | | 7 | Link (a tag) | An underlined bar of text. | The a tag makes a link, and its href attribute holds the address. | Write link text that says where the link goes. | | 8 | Table (table tag) | A small grid with two columns and three rows. | The table tag marks a table, and header cells use the th tag. | Mark header cells so screen readers can read the table. | **Provenance:** The tags follow the chapter section "HTML". The illustration is synthetic, and the sim labels the page "illustrative example". **Rules:** Each hint matches exactly one marker. The illustration contains no text, so every label comes from the table above. Markers are numbered 1 to 8 in the order of the table. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner hovers or clicks a marker and reads its label, description, and tip. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows a hint. 3. The learner clicks the marker they think the hint describes. 4. If the first click is wrong, the sim says so and lets the learner try once more. If the second click is also wrong, the sim reveals the marker and its description. 5. After all 8 hints the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 hints in a shuffled order, two attempts each. Only a correct first click counts as evidence. Correct: "Correct: [label]. [Description]". First wrong click: "Not quite. Look again at the hint: [hint]". Second wrong click: "This is [label]. [Description]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can read the parts of a page." Below 7 it lists the labels of the missed parts. **Starting State:** The illustration with eight numbered markers, explore mode active, and the prompt "Hover a marker to see which tag makes it." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says the heading tag marks a title, the paragraph tag marks text, the image tag has an alt attribute, and the link tag has an href attribute. The chapter's HTML example uses h1, p, img, and a.
